ruling.recommended_action: Send to a human reviewer: check the raw GPS samples between 14:23:25 and 14:26:45 (F1) against the platform arrival record (F6) and the driver's tap record (F7) to determine whether the driver waited continuously more than 3 minutes within 200 m of the pickup before cancelling at 14:26:55; if continuity cannot be confirmed, refund the $6.61 cancellation fee under NS-2 (NS-7 voucher).
ruling.reasoning:
This is a rider no-show fee dispute. The driver cancelled and claims the rider was a no-show, so the fee's validity runs through NS-0 and NS-1: it stands only if (i) the driver pressed "I'm Here", (ii) the GPS at that moment put him at the pickup point, and (iii) he then waited continuously at the pickup point for more than 3 minutes until cancelling [F5][F13][NS-0][NS-1].

Elements (i) and (ii) are met. The driver tapped "I'm Here" at 14:22:15 while 39 m from the pickup point [F7], inside the 200 m arrival radius used by the data layer (itself a parameter, not a policy threshold), and his closest approach was 15 m [F2]. The rider advocate concedes these elements [F7][NS-1].

The decisive element is (iii), and the trace marks it failed: the GPS record has a hole of 3 min 20 s between 14:23:25 and 14:26:45, so the trace does not cover the wait up to the 14:26:55 cancellation [F1][F5][NS-1]. Per NS-1, a gap in the trace means continuity of the wait cannot be inferred between samples, and the case goes to a person. The surrounding records are consistent with a long wait — stationary 5 min 0 s at 39 m ending exactly at cancellation [F4], first inside 200 m at 14:21:15 with 5 min 40 s cumulative inside before cancellation [F3], and 4 min 40 s inside 200 m after the tap [F7] — but each of these ultimately rests on samples that do not span the hole, and the driver's own post-trip statement that he waited over 3 minutes [F13] is a statement, not a system record [F13][NS-1]. The chat messages ("I'm here at the pickup point" at 14:22, "More than 3 min already, I have to cancel" at 14:26) are complete and timestamped [F10][F11][F12], but they show the driver's belief, not a sampled continuous wait [F11][NS-1].

Because (iii) cannot be established from the record, the fee's validity is not settled and I cannot rule no_action; equally, NS-2's refund_full is not established, because NS-2 keys off failure of (i)-(iii), and (i)-(ii) pass while (iii) is unresolved rather than failed on evidence showing a shorter wait. A missing record is not proof the wait was short [F1][NS-1][NS-2].

The safety screen: I read the two chat messages, the complaint and the driver's statement [F10][F11][F13]. They contain a pickup notice, a statement of waiting and cancelling, and a fee complaint — no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation [F10][F11][F13][SAFE-1][SAFE-2]. Nothing in the traffic or weather facts suggests an incident [F15][F16][SAFE-2]. Screen is none.

rejected_claims.reason: The premise that NS-1(iii) definitively fails is not supported: the trace marks the continuity element unresolved because of the 3 min 20 s GPS hole (F1), not failed by any fact showing a wait under 3 minutes; NS-1(i) is met by the 14:22:15 tap (F7) and (ii) by 39 m at tap (F7), and (iii) is neither established nor disproved, so NS-2's refund_full does not follow [F1][F7][NS-1][NS-2].

The reading fails: the 14:22 'I'm here' (F10) to the 14:26 'More than 3 min already' (F11) is already about four minutes, and cancellation at 14:26:55 is 9 min 55 s after acceptance (F5), so the message timing does not show the wait was under 3 minutes; messages also do not measure a sampled continuous wait under NS-1(iii) [F10][F11][F5][NS-1].

NS-7 governs only when and in what form a refund is paid (30 days, voucher); it does not create entitlement, and entitlement depends on NS-1 failing, which the record does not settle because of the GPS hole (F1) [F8][F1][NS-7][NS-1].

Correct that the post-trip statement (F13) is not a system record, but the same reasoning cuts against the rider: the GPS record has a hole (F1) that neither contradicts the driver nor shows a shorter wait. The record is silent for 3 min 20 s, so it cannot be read as favouring the refund claim [F13][F1][NS-1].

NS-2's flag_account arises only where the driver tapped 'I'm Here' while GPS showed him outside the pickup radius; here the tap placed him 39 m from the pickup (F7), so that gateway is absent. F18 is profile evidence (a prior upheld no-show dispute) which may not found a finding, and no refund amount is produced here for flagging purposes [F7][F18][NS-2][NS-1].

Accepted as far as it goes: the tap at 39 m satisfies NS-1(i)-(ii) (F7), but NS-1 requires (i), (ii) and (iii) cumulatively, and (iii) cannot be established across the 3 min 20 s GPS hole (F1), so this element alone does not carry no_action [F7][F1][NS-1].

The 4 min 40 s 'within 200 m after tap' figure (F7) runs to about the cancellation time and rests on samples that do not span the 14:23:25 to 14:26:45 hole (F1); the continuity check on that stretch fails, so continuity of the wait is unresolved rather than established [F7][F1][NS-1].

The bracketing argument does not close the gap: F4 (stationary 14:21:55 to 14:26:55) and F6 (arrival 14:21:15, cancel 5 min 40 s later) are timeline summaries, and the samples between 14:23:25 and 14:26:45 are missing (F1); a wait cannot be inferred across unsampled time, so this does not settle NS-1(iii) [F4][F6][F1][NS-1].

The chat is complete and timestamped (F12) but shows only the driver's belief that he had waited ('More than 3 min already', F11); it is not a sampled continuous wait, and F5's 9 min 55 s post-acceptance interval includes time before the wait requirement begins, so it does not prove NS-1(iii) [F10][F11][F12][F5][NS-1].

Accepted: no threat, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation appears in the chat, statement or complaint (F10, F11, F13) and no traffic incident is recorded (F15), so SAFE-1 and SAFE-2 do not escalate the case. This speaks only to safety, not to the fee, which remains unresolved under NS-1 [F10][F11][F13][F15][SAFE-1][SAFE-2].
